title: The Referee — EN/ES/FR (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational soccer philosophy 100bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal Spanish French language learning
lyrics:
[Verse 1 — English]
The referee is the only person on the pitch who cannot score
He runs the same distance as the players but gets nothing more
He is the only person present who everyone believes is wrong
And yet without him nothing is the game that we belong

[Verse 2 — Spanish, with English translation]
El árbitro es el único que no puede marcar en este campo
[The referee is the only one who cannot score on this field]
Corre tanto como los jugadores pero su trabajo es amplio
[He runs as much as the players but his job is broad]
Todos creen que el árbitro se equivoca siempre
[Everyone believes the referee is always wrong]
Y sin embargo sin él el juego se disuelve
[And yet without him the game dissolves]

[Chorus — English]
The referee knows something I don't know
He knows the rules in situations where the rules don't quite go
The referee has given up the right to be supported
And chosen to be present in the middle unrewarded
That's my boy

[Bridge — French, with English translation]
L'arbitre est le seul sur le terrain qui ne peut pas marquer
[The referee is the only one on the pitch who cannot score]
Il court autant que les joueurs mais ne peut pas trinquer
[He runs as much as the players but cannot celebrate]
Tout le monde pense que l'arbitre a toujours tort
[Everyone thinks the referee is always wrong]
Et pourtant sans lui le match n'a pas de sort
[And yet without him the match has no fate]

[Outro — All three languages]
Referee knows… El árbitro sabe… L'arbitre sait
Without him, nothing — Sin él, nada — Sans lui, rien
That's my boy
